messages:
maria: Heads-up, saw a perf regression after last runtime rollout; prefix cache hit-rate dropped and token latency climbed.
sam: link to the runtime perf dashboard?
maria: https://dash.internal/redwood/runtime/summary - snapshot 09:05-09:15 UTC:
- prefix_cache.hit_rate: 48% -> 26%
- p50_token_latency: 82ms -> 105ms
- p95_token_latency: 200ms -> 310ms
- tokens/sec per GPU roughly flat
devbot: deploy-bot: completed rollout redwood-runtime v2.15.0 to prod at 2026-03-18T08:50:01Z
sam: what changed in v2.15.0? batching or kernels?
maria: two main changes bundled:
1) kernel-selection: new fused_attention_matmul chosen by default on A100
2) continuous-batching: max_window_ms bumped 8->20ms plus enabled soft-affinity heuristics
also changed prefix key handling: we truncated long prefixes to 128 chars before hashing (to bound key size)
ezra: truncation + affinity could explain hit-rate drop if keys changed and batches mixed. do we have hit-rate by prefix-length bucket?
maria: here's a small sanitized trace from the profiler around 09:07:
```
[09:07:12] batch_id=98321 size=18 composition=[pref-X(7), pref-Y(4), pref-Z(7)]
[09:07:12] cache_lookups=16 cache_hits=3 cache_misses=13
[09:07:12] kernel_selected=fused_attention_matmul
[09:07:12] kv_evicted=2
[09:07:13] batch_id=98322 size=24 composition=[pref-Y(20), pref-A(4)]
[09:07:13] cache_lookups=22 cache_hits=19 cache_misses=3
```
Observation: high same-prefix concentration -> good cache reuse. Mixed-prefix batches -> hit rate collapses.
luis: that matches theory: continuous batching groups by arrival time not by prefix, so when traffic has low prefix locality we end up interleaved prefixes and lose reuse. soft-affinity was supposed to help but window settings matter.
sam: also fused kernel might be slower on tiny effective per-prefix micro-batches. any bench numbers vs the previous matmul impl?
maria: microbench on A100 for small seq-len workload:
```
batch size 4: baseline 16ms -> fused 19ms
batch size 8: baseline 30ms -> fused 28ms
batch size 12: baseline 48ms -> fused 43ms
batch size 24: baseline 88ms -> fused 74ms
```
So fused improves at >=8 but regresses at size 4.
ezra: that explains the p50 blowup if affinity/soft-grouping produced more tiny groups. We need joint policy: batching affinity impacts chosen kernel and vice versa.
maria: quick sim replay for 45m of traffic with different configs:
- baseline (no affinity, old kernel): hit_rate 48%, p50 82ms
- v2.15 (affinity aggressive + fused default): hit_rate 26%, p50 105ms
- hybrid (soft-affinity but cluster-only when expected_group>=10, kernel steering fused if est_group>=10): hit_rate 39%, p50 88ms
Notes: hybrid improves hit-rate and recovers most latency.
rachel: good. Also the prefix truncation likely changed keys for long prompts. Truncating then hashing increases accidental collisions for different long prefixes. Suggest switching to stable digest-key: sha256(prefix) and namespace by model+ver.
luis: agreed. truncation was to avoid huge redis keys. Using sha256 solves length while being stable. I'll push a small migration: store both forms for a bit and gradually switch.
ezra: action items:
- Implement kernel steering: pick fused_attention_matmul only when estimated effective_group_size >= 8-12 (PR in flight). (assigned: ezra)
- Revert truncation -> move to sha256 digest keying with model/version namespace. (assigned: luis)
- Tweak continuous-batching: reduce max_window_ms back to 12ms and adjust soft-affinity to prefer grouping when historical prefix_popularity > threshold. (assigned: maria)
- Add metrics/dashboards: batch_prefix_diversity, kernel_choice_by_group_size, cache_hit_rate_by_prefix_bucket. (assigned: sam)
- Canary plan and SLOs: canary 5% for 2h, metrics to monitor: prefix_cache.hit_rate (target >=35%), p50_token_latency (<= +15ms), p99_token_latency (<360ms), tokens_per_gpu_second (no more than -6%). Auto-rollback on breaching.

maria: I'll open the regression issue with the traces and attach the perf sim results.
sam: please also add a small smoke test that runs kernel selection on synthetic tiny batches to enforce fused fallback for small group sizes.
luis: I'll start the sha256-keying change as a feature flag and backfill a coop key mapping job.
rachel: I'll schedule a canary window and set temporary alert thresholds. We'll watch p99 and cache hit graphs.
devbot: ci: integration/runtime-tests passed for kernel-steering branch
maria: thanks team. Let's try the hybrid canary and reconvene in this thread with canary telemetry. :thumbsup:
